newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends mixed, March weak.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends mixed, March weak.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures ended mixed, with March weak on a perceived sudden increase in country movement and on slack export sales, traders said.

"I think the weakness in the March has to do with the fact that we don't have a lot of export business left and yet open interest is still pretty high, so maybe that's why we saw a liquidation of March longs," a trader said.

Posted receipts on the MGE cash trading floor showed 301 railcars of spring wheat. That marked an increase over previous days and was seen by some as a sign that the grain transportation headaches in the upper Midwest may be ebbing.
MGE spring wheat closed 3-1/4 cents per bushel lower to two cents higher, with March down 3-1/4 cents at $3.82-1/4.

The March/May spread erased nearly all of its gains over the past two days, closing at 17 cents after having widened Thursday to trade at 20 cents. Traders said locals were the biggest sellers of the spread, while flour mills were steady buyers of the March.
MGE barley futures closed four to five cents per cwt lower, with March down four cents at $6.51.
